newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia tariff moves not ideological - Hill.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia tariff moves not ideological - Hill.

text.p: Senior Australian government minister Robert Hill said on Thursday that decisions on tariffs affecting the car and textile industries would not be made on ideological grounds.
"The government is determined to ensure that Australia develops and retains strong and viable manufacturing industries," Hill, minister for the environment, told an economic forum in Adelaide.

"Decisions affecting various industries such as the car industry or the textile industry will not be made on ideological grounds or some narry ivory tower view which is out of touch with the real world," he said.

Hill's comments to a meeting of the Committee on Economic Development of Australia (CEDA) follow criticism by the car industry and South Australia and Victoria on a draft report on assistance to the automotive industry.

With tariffs due to drop to 15 percent by 2000, the industry is calling for a five-year freeze on further reductions, however the report by the Productivity Commission has proposed further cuts to five percent by 2004.
Speaking at the same forum, Graham Kraehe, managing director of diversified manufacturer Southcorp Holdings Ltd, said business leaders recognised tariffs should be reduced.
"But we do challenge the extent to which the government has adopted a 'lead the world' stance on trade liberalisation," he said.

Kraehe said any further unilateral reductions would be damaging and should only be contemplated in parallel with reductions in trade barriers, tariff and non-tariff, by Australia's major trading partners.
